brief: A Goldman Sachs cross-divisional chart selection dated 8 September 2026, compiled by Johannes Duttenhoefer. It reports and does not argue: each item is a standalone chart caption with no connecting thesis. Positioning: the GS prime book shows the US Fundamental Long/Short ratio and US net leverage both in the 4th percentile on a one-year horizon, and gold speculative positioning reversed sharply through late August on data to 25 August. Cross-region equity: capex drags US free cash flow yields versus Europe, US concentration remains much higher, European equity flows have been out of favour since 2020, and EUR investment grade and bond yields now compete with European dividends. Technology: AI company spending rose sharply, hyperscaler free cash flow is estimated negative through 2027 with a rebound in 2028, robot shipment forecasts quadruple, robot costs are set to fall 7 percent annually, AI task-completion horizons double every 7 months, DDR5 spot prices are rising, and the GSTMTMOM tech long/short momentum pair has drawn down about 50 percent since late-June highs. Also covered: private credit flow rebound and eased 2Q26 covenant defaults, French yields above Greece, 2025 effective tax rates, demographics, defence spending, streaming and dating engagement.
